2_Introduction: The PSCs demonstrated a champion PCE of 17.52%, with a VOC of 1.0523 V, JSC of 23.29 mA/cm², and FF of 71.52%. For the inorganic perovskite layers, 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 inorganic perovskite precursor solution was prepared in DMF/DMSO solvent. A sequential spin-coating procedure was employed, first at 1000 rpm for 10 s, followed by 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the last 6 s of the second step, 160 µL CB was dropped as antisolvent. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 277.88 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.28, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI₂. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI₂.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ inorganic perovskite is governed by a delicate interplay among A-site cation entropy (Cs⁺/MA⁺/FA⁺ mixing enhancing phase stability and suppressing δ-phase formation), B-site Pb²⁺ coordination dynamics, and X-site halide stoichiometry (Br⁻ incorporation tuning tolerance factor to ~0.98 and mitigating lattice strain), all of which collectively suppress ion migration and stabilize the black α-phase under thermal stress; the precisely timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene delivered during the final 6 s of high-speed spin-coating) critically arrests nucleation kinetics to yield uniform nuclei density, while the 110 °C/25 min annealing profile promotes Ostwald ripening without inducing halide segregation or PbI₂ volatilization—evidenced by XRD showing only a weak residual PbI₂ peak at 12.65° (277.88 cts, FWHM = 0.28°), confirming near-complete conversion of the precursor into phase-pure perovskite with minimal lattice disorder and low microstrain, thereby reducing trap-assisted recombination centers at grain boundaries and within the bulk; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or molecular passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the optimized A-site cation alloying—which passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ via FA⁺-induced lattice relaxation and Cs⁺-mediated surface stabilization—and the Br⁻-driven tightening of the conduction band minimum, which synergistically elevates the quasi-Fermi level splitting and suppresses non-radiative voltage losses; the structural integrity inferred from the narrow PbI₂ FWHM and low residual intensity directly correlates with enhanced carrier diffusion length and reduced interfacial recombination, as further implied by the high VOC of 1.0523 V, JSC of 23.29 mA/cm², FF of 71.52%, and champion PCE of 17.52%.
